11tq9ypkwh6: ## Why the key is a critical secret
1lvl4etpo21: A recovery key unlocks the disk. Lost, it makes the data inaccessible; poorly protected, it becomes a back door for whoever obtains the device. It must therefore be **backed up reliably** and its **access limited**. Before enabling BitLocker, plan recovery: who can obtain a key, after which identity verification, and how it is audited.
21160y0x5j4: For silent encryption, recovery keys are **backed up automatically to Microsoft Entra ID** at encryption time. Verify: successful Entra join (condition for automatic escrow), no policy conflict that blocks the backup, and that escrow works in the **encryption report**. A useful setting: **Store recovery information in Entra before enabling BitLocker** set to Required, so that encryption does not start without a backup. For tenant-attached devices, Intune can display key data depending on Configuration Manager version and role prerequisites.
v4r1bbrpfa: A recovery key that has been used once is known by at least one person. **Client-driven automatic rotation** replaces the recovery password after it has been used to unlock the drive (Entra joined or hybrid joined devices). The Intune remote action **BitLocker key rotation** also makes it possible to trigger one. Prerequisites: Windows 10 version 1909 or later, or Windows 11; rotation enabled by the policy ("Client-driven recovery password rotation"), "Save BitLocker recovery information to Microsoft Entra ID" enabled and "Store recovery information… before enabling BitLocker" required. The roles with the **Rotate BitLockerKeys** right under "Remote tasks" include Help Desk Operator and Endpoint Security Administrator.
2fcych3f3d3: Give the right to read or rotate keys to the **smallest number of roles** necessary, and treat each lookup as a sensitive event to audit. Level 1 support does not need the rotation right if an escalation procedure exists. These choices are documented in the configuration sheet (21 points) under "recovery".
1vfjm9vkqik: Deleting the Intune object of an Entra-joined device protected by BitLocker triggers a sync that **removes the key protectors from the system volume** and leaves BitLocker **suspended** on that volume: a cleanup deletion is therefore not harmless. A **firmware update** can trigger recovery: suspend BitLocker beforehand, then resume protection afterwards. If recovery takes place, the password can be used and the platform validation profile is updated to avoid the next recovery.

1xjr56qs6v9: ## Read a password: rights and audit
1nxea785ze6: Reading the password requires the action `microsoft.directory/deviceLocalCredentials/password/read`. 1van2tg7ujl: ## What EPM is and what it costs
2alytcewaik: Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) lets users work **without administrator rights** and elevate **just-in-time** specific files approved by IT (installations, drivers, diagnostics). Each elevation is logged with metadata. **Nature: add-on feature under additional license.** EPM must be licensed in the tenant, alone or in the Intune suite; the offers change, so validate the advanced features page at each review. Windows only. Notably supported are the single-session virtual machines of Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 (see the FAQ).
14fpxcdkcqw: The **elevation settings policy** enables EPM on the device, sets the **default response** for any file without a rule and configures the data sent for reports. Its settings are **device-scope**: they apply to all users of the device, even if it is assigned to a user group. Do not therefore assign different policies to user groups to switch the default response by user. The **elevation rules policy** identifies specific files or scripts and the associated action; one policy accepts up to **100 rules**. The supported files are `.exe` executables, `.msi` installers and `.ps1` PowerShell scripts.
